answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down; shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five face down on top; shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one face down on top. The deck has 10 cards, with I on top, then five II, then four III. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Shuffle the four Conflict III cards… Shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five… Shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one… Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In a four-player game, a human starts at 1 VP; in a three-player game, at 0 VP. In both, take two Agents on the Leader and put the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; start with three troops in the garrison and the remaining nine troops in supply; take 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Place one of your two discs on the Score track — on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space’; ‘Place two Agents on your Leader and your third Agent… next to the game board’; ‘three… [troops] in… garrisons… remaining nine… in your supply’; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the Reveal boxes of cards just revealed, not cards played on Agent turns. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase’; Reveal Turn: ‘Reveal box effects of the just-revealed cards only (not of cards played on Agent turns)’ and ‘Move all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.’

answers.answer: No. The destination cost must be paid immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the played card, so that card’s Agent-box effect cannot first provide the resources. One card can send only one Agent, using only one of its Agent icons. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs must be paid ‘immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played)’; ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents’; a card with no Agent icons ‘can't be played on an Agent turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space you can deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for up to five total. At a non-Combat destination you cannot deploy units. Recruited troops are taken from your supply and placed in your garrison; at a Combat space, troops recruited during that turn may then be deployed.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: the cube icon takes a troop ‘from your supply and place[s] it in your garrison’; at a Combat space deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn… plus up to two more units from your garrison.’ Board Space Guide: ‘spaces not marked Combat do not’ permit normal deployment.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you already have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate lets you recall your Spy from a connected post to send an Agent to an opponent-occupied space. Gather Intelligence lets you recall a connected Spy when sending an Agent and draw a card; choose to do so immediately after placing the Agent, before receiving space or card effects. One Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though two different Spies can be used for those two different effects on one placement. You cannot use two Spies to Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon lets you send to a connected space and ‘do not recall the Spy’; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence are described separately. Gather Intelligence is decided ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)’; ‘You cannot recall the same Spy to both’ effects; FAQ: ‘never two to Gather Intelligence on the same placement.’

answers.answer: Your strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four revealed swords 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0 even if swords were revealed. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window, which is limited to players with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: ‘Each troop… 2… each sandworm = 3… each sword… = 1’; ‘You must have at least one unit… if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.’ Combat Intrigue is for each player with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict.’

answers.answer: Yes. Passing earlier does not prevent you from playing Combat Intrigue later in the phase. The window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, at which point Combat resolves. After rewards, troops in the Conflict return to their supply (not their garrison), and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve once players ‘pass consecutively.’ Cleanup: troops return to ‘supply (not their garrison)’ and sandworms return to the bank.

answers.answer: For any number of players tied for first, each gets the second reward; no one wins the Conflict or takes its card. In a three-player game, no other rewards are given. In a four-player game, if exactly two tie for first, the remaining players compete for the third reward; if three or more tie for first, there are no other rewards. A player at zero strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: ‘they each gain the second reward, and no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; three or fewer players get no other rewards; in four players, exactly two tied leave others to compete for third, but three or more tied means no other rewards. Resolve Combat: ‘A player with 0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double the rewards taken; having two sandworms does not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. If a reward offers 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time to take that reward again: pay another 3 spice for a second VP, or 6 spice total for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more sandworms… double’; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. For an optional cost, ‘you may pay the cost a second time to gain it a second time,’ with the example of paying 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2.

answers.answer: Check for a normal match after the Conflict winner takes that card into their supply. It can match another face-up Conflict or Objective card in that supply with the same Crysknife, Desert Mouse, or Ornithopter icon. A normal match is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During the Endgame, you may match the wild icon with any one of the three icons in your supply, flipping that pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card, check for another ‘face-up Conflict or Objective card’ with the same icon; if present, you ‘must’ flip the pair and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, you ‘may match the wild battle icon.’

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose it if Influence drops below 2 and regain it on reaching 2 again. At 4, the printed track bonus is retained if you later fall below 4 and is earned again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also gains the Alliance token and 1 VP, but that VP follows possession of the token. Tying the holder at 4 does not take it; an opponent must rise higher. If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes it; falling to 3 or less also loses it, returning it to the board if no one with 4+ can take it.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: at 2, gain 1 VP and ‘lose it below 2 and regain it when reaching 2 again’; at 4, track bonus is kept below 4 and earned again on return. ‘Tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance’; FAQ: holder Influence loss after a tie transfers it to a formerly tied player; falling to 3 or lower loses it, and it returns to board if nobody with 4+ can take it.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn you may spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card and split a single source across different cards; unused Persuasion is lost. The Row is replenished immediately to five cards, so you may buy a replacement card in the same Reveal turn if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile and are not used immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal effects: spend Persuasion ‘before, between, or after’ effects. Acquiring Cards: may pool sources or split a source; Row ‘must always have five cards’ and ‘after acquiring a card you may acquire its replacement’; acquired card goes face up into discard.

answers.answer: In the Makers phase, each Agent-free Maker space—Deep Desert, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin—gets 1 spice from the bank in its bonus spot, accumulating with prior bonus spice; an Agent visiting gains all bonus spice there. While the Shield Wall remains, sandworms cannot be summoned to a Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin; a detonation effect removes the token and then permits summoning there. A sandworm icon usually requires Maker Hooks, but Hooks are not universal if the summoning effect does not specify them. Hooks are retained, not spent. A sandworm is summoned straight to your quadrant of the Conflict and can never be placed in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers: each Maker space with no Agent gets ‘1 spice… in its bonus-spice spot’; sending an Agent gains ‘all the bonus spice.’ Sandworms: Hooks are usually required, not universal, and ‘never spent’; a sandworm is immediately deployed to the Conflict and ‘can never be placed in a garrison.’ Shield Wall protects the three named locations until removed.

answers.answer: Endgame is triggered at the end of a round if any player has at least 10 VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Before comparing scores, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards. Most VP wins; ties are broken in order by spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Game end: ‘At the end of a round’ with 10+ VP or an empty Conflict Deck; first players may resolve Endgame Intrigue, then highest VP wins; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup uses 20 contracts: two are face up on the board and the remaining 18 are face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue cards and four Imperium cards to their respective decks. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left in the box and are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: shuffle 20, ‘flip two face up,’ place ‘remaining 18 face down’; shuffle four additional Intrigue and four Imperium cards into decks; Shaddam is ‘not required.’ Scope and CHOAM section say the 10 contrasting-back contracts are only a Rise of Ix compatibility set and ‘leave them in the box.’

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon means take one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replace it from the bank, face up. If all contracts have been taken by players, it instead gives 2 Solari. Complete a Harvest contract by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the specified total spice that turn, including spice from other sources; complete an Immediate contract as soon as taken; complete an Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take one face-up, replace it from bank; if all taken, ‘reverts to giving 2 Solari.’ Completing contracts defines Harvest as gaining the shown total spice during a Maker visit, Immediate as completed on taking, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow as completed when next acquiring that card.

answers.answer: No. You must have held a board-space contract when sending the Agent there; if you acquire it after already sending an Agent to that space this turn, wait until a future turn. On completion, announce it, gain its listed rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: if you take a contract for a space where you ‘already sent your Agent this turn,’ you ‘must wait until a future turn’; you must have held it when sending the Agent. On completion, ‘announce it, gain the rewards it shows, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.’

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. Give the Rival the Ornithopter Objective; randomly deal the other two eligible Objectives to the humans, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective starts. First Player alternates only between the humans. Each round’s order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival takes Agent turns but never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival: ‘one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor’; give it Ornithopter and deal the other two Objectives to humans, with First Player assigned by the marker; ‘First Player alternates only between humans’; order First Player → Rival → other human; Rival ‘never takes a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: The Rival ignores an occupied destination and reveals another House Hagal card. If that next card is Place Spy, it places a Spy at an empty observation post of the specified type; if none exists, it ignores the placement. Because Place Spy did not send an Agent, it reveals another Hagal card either way. Rivals ignore normal board-space costs and effects, applying only the Hagal effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Agent turns: ‘Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again’; empty House Hagal or Reshuffle means ‘immediately reshuffle it and continue.’ Rival rules: ignore normal space costs/effects. Place Spy: use an empty specified post or ignore placement if none; ‘either way reveal another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent.’
